title: Lemon Dijon Butter Basa
description: Pan-seared basa fillets finished in a glossy lemon, garlic and dijon butter sauce. Light, quick, and no cream needed.

ingredients.notes: for dusting if required, read step 1 in the method
fresh is best, bottled works well too

method.instruction: Pat the basa fillets dry and season with salt and white pepper. Choose your style now, before going further: Option 1: Leave the fillets whole, dust them lightly in the plain flour, shaking off excess, and continue to step 2. Option 2: Cut into pieces roughly 1 inch (2.5 cm) thick, skip the flour entirely and skip ahead to step 4.
Melt half the butter in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear the basa for about 2 minutes per side until golden and just cooked through. Remove and set aside.

If seared: lower the heat to medium and add the remaining butter to the same pan. If poaching from raw: melt all the butter in the pan over medium heat. Either way, add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Stir in the dijon mustard, lemon juice, chicken stock, brown sugar and smoked paprika. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until slightly reduced and glossy - get it to the consistency you want now, as it won't reduce much further once the fish is in.

If seared: return the basa to the pan, spooning the sauce over, and warm through for 1 minute without breaking up the pieces. If poaching from raw: gently lower the basa into the sauce, don't stir, and spoon sauce over the top to baste. Poach for 4 to 5 minutes until just opaque and flaking. Serve straight from the pan over rice.

notes.title: Handling the Fish
notes.content: Basa cooks fast and flakes easily. If poaching, handle it gently once it's in the sauce - spoon liquid over rather than stirring or flipping, so the pieces hold together.

notes.title: The Sauce
notes.content: Built in the same pan the fish was seared in (if going that route) so it picks up the browned bits - don't wipe the pan out.

notes.title: Serving
notes.content: Good served over rice or with steamed greens, spooning the sauce over both.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Best eaten fresh - the fish texture suffers on reheating. Refrigerate covered for up to 1 day if needed.
